Synopsis:
The player has accepted a invitation from Gale's hologram projection to come meet the real Gale at a secluded grove at night. There, they speak about how this may be his last night alive, as they near the heart of the Absolute, where Gale is destined to blow himself up. The player probes his mindset and can try to comfort him. Ultimately the scene may become romantic. Gale may lead the player to a magically-infused sex scene amidst the stars, or the player may determine they should take a more grounded approach.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_GalesLastNightAlive_SD_ROM.json: The player has accepted Gale’s holographic invitation and met the real Gale in a secluded, shadow‑cursed grove at night; Gale has fashioned a spectacular, magical sky (aurora and will‑o'‑wisps) to make the evening special. Off‑screen: the party is approaching the heart of the Absolute, and Gale believes he is fated to die there — possibly by detonating himself — so he recruited this last quiet night to speak frankly and, perhaps, say goodbye. The two share a close relationship (the scene can turn intimate or remain consolatory), and the player can probe his mindset, offer comfort, or pursue a romantic/sexually magical encounter Gale may initiate. Other camp events or companions may exist elsewhere, but they do not directly affect this private, emotionally charged meeting.
- CAMP_Gale_CRD_SpellTeaching.json: In this scene, Gale is conjuring an image of Mystra over the palm of his hand, staring at the goddess he’s love with, but who abandoned him. When the player approaches, he dispels the image and he feels embarrassed to have been caught doing what he was doing. The conversation turns to his passion for magic however, and he invites the player to try to cast a spell with him together. The player can do so by passing through various stages of spell casting, and when successful, this can lead to a first player-initiated romantic moment with Gale.

context: The player accepted Gale’s holographic invitation and met the real Gale alone in a secluded, shadow‑cursed grove at night; Gale has created a spectacular, magical sky (aurora and will‑o’‑wisps) to make the evening special. Off‑screen, the rest of the party is closing on the heart of the Absolute, and Gale believes he is fated to die there—possibly by detonating himself—so he asked for this last quiet night to speak frankly and, perhaps, say goodbye. The two share a close relationship: Gale can be wistful or embarrassed (he sometimes conjures an image of Mystra and quickly dispels it) and he may invite the player to try casting with him. Depending on the player’s choices, the scene can remain consolatory or develop into shared spellcasting that leads to a romantic, magically infused intimate encounter; other companions and camp events are off‑screen and don’t affect this private moment.
